meta.title: Storm Harbor — Continuous Disaster Recovery Readiness
meta.description: Discover dependencies, prove recoverability, and orchestrate auditable recovery across Terraform, Google Cloud, Kubernetes, and GitOps.

hero.title: Recovery stops being
hero.body: Storm Harbor connects code, cloud, clusters, backups, and policy into one continuously reconciled view of what can recover — and what stands in the way.

integrations.label: Federates the tools you already run

problem.title: A runbook is not proof.
problem.body: Repositories describe intent. APIs expose actual state. Backups live elsewhere. Test evidence is scattered across pipelines and tickets. Storm Harbor correlates those fragments without taking authority away from the systems that own them.
problem.question: Can this service recover now, within its agreed RTO and RPO?

capabilities.title: Know. Prove. Recover.
capabilities.body: Move from disconnected disaster-recovery plans to a living, evidence-driven operating model.
capabilities.discoverBody: Build a service-first inventory and typed dependency graph from GitHub, Terraform, GCP, Kubernetes, and GitOps — with provenance and freshness attached.
capabilities.proveBody: Evaluate coverage, drift, recovery points, access, test recency, and measured objectives. A score never hides a mandatory blocked gate.
capabilities.orchestrateBody: Freeze immutable revisions, execute idempotent phases through health gates, stop safely, and preserve cleanup and evidence on every outcome.

dashboard.graphAriaLabel: Dependency graph connecting authoritative sources to recovery evidence

readiness.title: A score with consequences.
readiness.body: See the headline without losing the engineering truth underneath. Storm Harbor keeps binary controls visible, explains every finding, and shows exactly why a service is blocked.
readiness.pointOne: Service-level RTO and RPO tied to actual recovery points
readiness.pointTwo: Every relationship includes source, confidence, and observed time
readiness.pointThree: Signed evidence links input, decision, actor, action, and outcome

architecture.title: Federated by design. Outside the blast radius.
architecture.body: Each system remains authoritative in its own domain. The control plane materializes a current operational index, freezes a recovery plan, and coordinates work through versioned adapters.
architecture.sourcesBody: Read desired state, runtime state, policies, and recovery points where they live.
architecture.controlBody: Normalize assets, map dependencies, evaluate freshness, drift, and policy.
architecture.recoverBody: Execute idempotent phases with approvals, timeouts, allowlists, and a kill switch.
architecture.proofBody: Measure objectives and retain signed, immutable evidence outside the failure domain.
architecture.outside: The recovery brain runs outside the cluster it may need to rebuild.

principles.title: Safe by architecture, not convention.
principles.body: Real recovery is never enabled implicitly. Permissions are short-lived, decisions fail closed, and every mutation is interruptible and auditable.
principles.federatedBody: Git, cloud APIs, vaults, and evidence stores keep ownership of their own domains.
principles.identityBody: OIDC and workload identity replace persistent cloud keys and phase-wide credentials.
principles.closedBody: Missing evidence, stale data, policy failure, or an unavailable source never appears healthy.
principles.evidenceBody: Inputs, policy decisions, timing, actions, and outcomes are linked and integrity checked.

audience.title: One view. Different decisions.
audience.body: Technical depth for the people who recover systems; clear outcomes for the people accountable for continuity.
audience.platformBody: Map Terraform, GCP, GKE, and GitOps into repeatable recovery paths without replacing existing workflows.
audience.sreBody: Exercise runbooks, expose dependency gaps, and measure recovery objectives from real checkpoints.
audience.riskBody: Trace each decision to its source, policy, approval, identity, evidence, and immutable revision.
audience.leadersBody: Prioritize investment with a service-level view of readiness, blockers, and test recency.

openSource.title: Inspect the recovery brain.
openSource.body: Critical continuity infrastructure should be understandable, extensible, and reviewable. Explore the architecture, run safe simulations, and help shape provider contracts in the open.

finalCta.title: Make recoverability a fact.
finalCta.body: Start with the architecture and safe simulation scaffold. See how Storm Harbor turns fragmented state into continuous recovery readiness.

footer.tagline: Discover dependencies. Prove recoverability. Orchestrate recovery.
